concept.name: Predicted funding rate
concept.definition: The predicted (estimated) funding rate is the exchange's real-time forecast of the funding rate that will apply at the next funding timestamp, computed from the premium index samples collected so far in the current interval.
concept.intuition: It is the meter running on the next funding bill: it shows what longs or shorts would pay if the interval ended right now.
concept.mechanics: Binance continuously samples the premium index (impact bid/ask vs price index, roughly every minute) over the current 8-hour window; the displayed predicted rate is the estimate from samples to date — note the convention that the rate shown at e.g. 09:00 UTC uses the premium dataset from 01:00 to 09:00, not just the final hour. The realized rate is fixed only at the funding timestamp.
concept.formula: Predicted funding ≈ time-weighted average of premium index samples in the current interval + interest component (venue-specific).
concept.failure_modes: The prediction moves with order-book depth: thin or spoofed books late in the interval can swing the final rate away from hours of stable estimates, so positioning on the predicted rate carries estimate risk.
concept.misconceptions: The predicted rate is not locked in — only the rate at the funding timestamp applies, and late premium swings can change it materially. A persistent large prediction is a signal about crowded positioning, not a guaranteed payment.
concept.example: If the premium index has averaged +0.02% through six hours of the interval, the predicted funding shows ~+0.02%+interest; a sharp sell-off in the last hour can drag the realized rate to +0.005% instead.

citations.source: Binance Support - Introduction to Binance Futures Funding Rates
